# tiny-trace-otel

> A tiny, stdlib-only OpenTelemetry-compatible OTLP/HTTP tracing exporter for Python.
> W3C Trace Context, OTLP/JSON envelopes, batch processor. ~440 lines. Zero deps.

## What it is
The smallest way to ship OpenTelemetry-compatible spans from Python without
pulling in the ~6MB `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http` package.
Drops a `Tracer` and `BatchSpanProcessor` with synchronous OTLP/HTTP
export into any collector (Honeycomb, SigNoz, Tempo, Datadog, Jaeger).

## When to use it
- You're shipping traces from a Python service and don't want 6MB of deps for one POST.
- You want OTLP/HTTP JSON wire-format compat with all major backends.
- You want a `with span:` block that auto-ends + auto-records exceptions.
- You want W3C Trace Context parse/format helpers for cross-service propagation.

## When NOT to use it
- You need gRPC OTLP — this is HTTP/JSON only (by design).
- You push >10k spans/sec — use the official OTel SDK which streams gRPC.
- You need metrics or logs (only traces here; see `tiny-cost-tracker` for cost-only metrics).

## Public API
- `Tracer(name, resource_attrs=None, parent_context=None)`
  - `start_span(name, kind="INTERNAL", attributes=None, parent=None) -> Span`
- `Span(context, name, kind=...)`
  - `set_attribute(k, v)`, `set_attributes({...})`, `add_event(name, **attrs)`
  - `set_status(status, message=None)` — `StatusCode.{UNSET, OK, ERROR}`
  - `record_exception(exc)` — adds event + sets ERROR
  - `end(status=None, message=None)`
  - `with s:` context manager
  - `to_otel_dict() -> dict` — OTLP JSON wire format
- `SpanKind.{INTERNAL, SERVER, CLIENT, PRODUCER, CONSUMER}`
- `SpanContext(trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id=None, trace_flags="01", trace_state="", is_remote=False)`
- `OTLPHttpExporter(endpoint, headers, timeout_seconds=5.0)`
  - `export(spans) -> (http_status, error_or_None)`
- `StdoutExporter(stream=None)` for local debug
- `BatchSpanProcessor(exporter, max_queue_size=1024, max_batch_size=64, export_interval_seconds=2.0, export_timeout_seconds=30.0)`
  - `on_end(span)`, `force_flush()`, `shutdown(timeout_seconds=None)`
  - `dropped_count` — spans dropped due to queue overflow
- `parse_traceparent(value) -> SpanContext` — W3C parse
- `format_traceparent(trace_id, span_id, flags="01") -> str` — W3C format
- `get_tracer(name="tiny-trace-otel") -> Tracer` — singleton
- `set_processor(processor) -> Token` / `reset_processor(token)` — active processor
- `TraceError` — raised on malformed headers / unknown status

## Wire format
OTLP/HTTP JSON envelopes per the official specification. Spans serialise
via `to_otel_dict()`. Resource attributes are prefixed with `process.*`
(then de-prefixed by the exporter when it builds the envelope).

## Threading
- Sync API; for asyncio, wrap `with tracer.start_span(...)` in `asyncio.to_thread`.
- `BatchSpanProcessor` runs one daemon worker thread.
- `OTLPHttpExporter` uses `urllib.request`, which releases the GIL during I/O.

## Installation
```bash
pip install tiny-trace-otel
# or vendor the single file
```

## Common pitfalls
- `SpanContext.parent_span_id` must be 16 lowercase hex chars or None.
- `traceparent` flags byte MUST be 2 lowercase hex chars; only `01` (sampled) is meaningful here.
- OTLP envelope requires `resourceSpans[].scopeSpans[].spans[]` even if you ship 1 span.
- Status code `0` (UNSET) is the default; `2` (ERROR) overrides on exception via `record_exception`.

## Integration with OpenClaw ecosystem
- `tiny-cost-tracker` — its `Span("charge")` can set attribute `cost.usd`.
- `tiny-budget-ledger` — gate every span on `can_spend()` before opening.
- `tiny-otel` (Node.js) — sibling JS library; same wire format.
- `tiny-mcp-server` / `tiny-mcp-client` — wrap MCP traffic in OTLP spans.

## Version
0.1.0 (2026-09-16)
